gameplay_summary: Feature-packed baseball with 16 teams and a 'parent and child' cartridge system: plug cheap data cartridges into a slot on the back to update player rosters, then play pennant races, versus games, team editing and events.
dossier: Sunsoft's baseball game, the first to use its 'twin cassette' system. The main cartridge (the 'parent turtle') has a slot on its back for small, cheap 'child turtle' cartridges that update the player data, so the game could in theory be kept current indefinitely. There are 12 teams modelled on the real pro clubs plus four originals, four parks, and a pennant race of 30 to 130 games leading to the Japan Series and a hidden SS team. Rule tweaks, day or night games, brawls, fine plays, training, stat growth and items bought with earnings are all included, and the balance favours hitters. Swapping child cartridges wipes save data.

gameplay_summary: Monopoly-style board game with stocks: roll around five boards buying shops, charging rivals who land on them, investing in districts, and visiting the four suit marks to build total assets and return to the bank.

gameplay_summary: Grid puzzle: as a jewel holding a weakened goddess, hop across an 8×8 temple floor, stepping on arrows to shift rows and columns so matching objects meet and vanish, until the board is clear.
dossier: Human's object-elimination puzzle game. An Indiana Jones-style explorer trapped in an ancient Egyptian temple meets a goddess so drained of power that she can only exist as a big spherical jewel, and enters it to restore her by clearing each stage. On an 8×8 grid of empty spaces, walls, objects and arrows, you move the jewel freely except through walls. Stepping on an arrow slides its row or column in that direction, and lining up two or more matching objects erases them. Clear every object to finish the stage.
